Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the Global Consumer Brands Inc. Q3 FY2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. If you would like to ask a question at that time, please press star one on your telephone keypad and wait for your name to be announced. To withdraw your question, press star two. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss Global Consumer Brands Inc.'s Q3 FY2024 results. With me on the call are Mark Rivera, Chief Executive Officer; Sarah Thompson, Chief Financial Officer; Lisa Chen, Chief Marketing Officer; and David Lopez, Chief Supply Chain Officer; and other members of our leadership team.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that some of the statements we will be making today are forward-looking and are based on our current expectations and beliefs. These statements are subject to certain risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed description of these risks and uncertainties.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Mark Rivera.

Mark Rivera:
Thank you, Alex. Good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us. Global Consumer Brands delivered a solid Q3, demonstrating the resilience of our brands and the strength of our team. We are navigating a dynamic environment and remain focused on executing our strategic priorities.

Our discussion today will cover six key aspects: new product launches and innovation pipeline update; decomposition of organic sales growth into volume, price, and mix; summary of financial results and outlook; market share trends by category and region; gross margin guidance and key assumptions; and A&P spend and ROI.

I will now turn the call over to Sarah Thompson to provide more detail on our financial results.

Sarah Thompson:
Thank you, Mark. As Mark mentioned, we delivered a solid quarter. Net sales were $14.2 billion, representing a 5.2% increase compared to the prior year. This included 5.2% organic growth, blending 2.1% volume/mix and 2.6% pricing actions. Gross margin was 48.7%, driven by productivity savings, pricing discipline, and favorable mix. Adjusted operating income was $3.18 billion, up 9% year-over-year. Adjusted diluted earnings per share were $1.48, up 8.7%. We continue to manage our costs effectively and invest in our long-term growth initiatives.

Let me start with a deeper summary of our financial results and outlook, which highlight the resilience of our diverse portfolio spanning personal care like VitalShine shampoos and GlowEssence skincare, household essentials such as CleanSweep detergents, and nutritionals including NutriBoost protein bars and PureFlow beverages. This marks our sixth straight quarter of positive organic sales growth, outpacing the broader CPG category, which grew just 2.1% globally per NielsenIQ data. We beat our EPS guidance midpoint by $0.03 despite $0.05 FX headwinds from a stronger dollar against the euro and emerging currencies.

Organic growth was broad-based. Beverages rose 6.1%, with HydroSpark zero-sugar electrolytes up 15% on expanded Walmart and Amazon Fresh distribution. Snacks and confectionery gained 4.2% organically via pricing and premiumization, with CleanCrunch nut bars capturing 2.5 share points in better-for-you per IRI. Personal care was 2.9% organic, offset by double-digit growth in EcoLocks sustainable haircare.

Gross margin expanded 210 basis points from our $450 million Project Horizon productivity program across 150 plants, including $180 million procurement savings on cocoa and palm oil. Pricing added 140 basis points, logistics deflation 70. Adjusted operating margin rose 110 basis points to 22.4%, with A&P at 12.1% of sales shifted to high-ROI digital yielding 3.2x returns.

North America led with 7.4% organic on 4.1% volumes in club channels like Costco. EMEA grew 2.1% amid UK/Germany inflation. Asia-Pacific hit 5.6% on China snacks. Latin America steady at 3.2%. Operating cash flow was $2.1 billion, up 14%, funding $1.2 billion repurchases and dividends—our 62nd year of increases. Net debt to EBITDA at 2.1x supports M&A in plant-based.

Under Power Up 2025, we're launching 25 health & wellness innovations, growing e-commerce to 18%, and hitting 45% recycled packaging for 50% by 2025, boosting brand scores 12 points per Kantar.

For Q4, organic sales 3-4%, EPS $1.55-$1.60; full-year organic 3.5-4.5%, EPS $5.92-$6.00, midpoint up $0.10. FY2025 organic 4%+, with mid-48% gross margins.

Now, turning to the decomposition of our organic sales growth. This 5.2%—fifth consecutive positive quarter—excludes acquisitions, divestitures, FX. It breaks into volume +2.1%, pricing +2.5%, mix +0.6%.

Volume +2.1% beat category averages, led by household/personal care +3.4% on 150 bps ACV gains to 92% in Walmart/Kroger. CleanSweep laundry pods up 8% units on concentrate-to-save messaging amid 15% laundry cost hikes. Nutritionals flat on premium protein fatigue like Clif/Quest, offset by PureFlow +5% in convenience to 14% share.

North America +2.8% via AI trade optimization improving promo ROI 12%. Europe flat on private label shifts. Emerging +4.2%, Latin America +7% via Brazil micro-depots at 45,000 outlets.

Pricing +2.5%, in line with 2-3% guide, recovering 4.1% input inflation (palm +22%, PET +18%). Cumulative +18% since FY22 restores margins to 48.2%, up 110 bps QoQ. Mix-neutral: +3.2% mass personal care, steady premium. North America +3.1% on retailer alignment, emerging +3.7% with India compliance tech.

Our Pricing Analytics Platform simulates 50,000 scenarios per SKU for 65% COGS recovery, -0.3% volume drag vs. industry -1.2%.

Mix +0.6% from power brands at 82% sales. Personal care +1.2% on GlowEssence 12% growth. Nutritionals +0.8% PowerPack bundles. North America +0.9%, emerging +1.4% Asia skincare.

Focus 20 pruned 20% low-margin SKUs, reinvesting $150M. Q4 guide: organic 4-6%, volume +1.5-2.5%, pricing +2-2.5%, mix +0.5-1%.

Next, our gross margin guidance and key assumptions. Q3 was 45.2%, up 110 bps YoY/40 bps QoQ on moderating inputs like cocoa (-15% off highs), palm, dairy; +3.5% AUR pricing; premium mix.

FY2024 guide 45.5-46.0%, Q4 46.0-46.5%. Drivers: inputs neutral to +20 bps with 80% 2025 hedged 5-7% below spot; pricing +80-100 bps at 3-4%, PCU >1.05x; mix +40-60 bps with I&R 22% sales; supply chain +30-50 bps via AI demand sensing cutting inventory 12%, waste 8%, utilization 88%.

North America 47.0-47.5%, EMEA 43.5-44.0%, LATAM 44.0-44.5%, APAC 46.5-47.0%. Risks: 10% USD strength -20-30 bps, geopolitics +50 bps friction.

Finally, A&P spend and ROI. Q3 A&P $452 million, +6% YoY, 11.8% sales: $190M advertising +12%, $262M promo flat. Blended ROMI 2.7x, +14%, vs. 2.5x benchmark.

Digital 35% media mix at 4.1x ROMI, RMNs like Walmart Connect/Amazon DSP; CrunchTime snacks campaign 3.2x, 25 bps share gain. Trade TPE 92%, velocity +4% ACV. North America 3.0x, Europe 2.2x, emerging 3.4x India/Brazil.

A&P 360 platform with Google Cloud AI enables 20% faster iterations. Q4 12.2% sales, 2.8x ROMI on holidays.

With that financial overview, I'll turn the call over to Lisa to discuss brand performance, innovation, and market share.

Lisa Chen:
Thank you, Sarah. We saw strong performance in our core brands. Let me provide an update on new product launches and our innovation pipeline, a cornerstone for top-line growth in a 2-3% category world per IRI/Nielsen, against P&G, Unilever, Mondelez pressures.

Q3 launches: 12 SKUs across beauty/personal care, nutritionals, household—+25% NPD velocity. Contributed 2.5 points to 5.2% organic, 65% repeat rates vs. 50% hurdle/45% industry.

VitaGlow Probiotic Skincare: $45M sales, 120% forecast, 8,500 U.S. ACV, 2.1 points in $12B serums per Circana, 52% margins via Copenhagen fermentation -18% costs.

NutriBoost Functional Beverages: $32M, +150% seq., 35% e-comm Shopee/Lazada, 1.8 China penetration, TikTok 2.5x ROI in $25B APAC market.

EcoShield Cleaners: $28M, 15% Mexico trial Walmart/Soriana, 100% PCR packaging, 22% repeat on eco-shift (75% U.S. priority per NielsenIQ).

Pipeline: $285M R&D nine months +15% YoY, 3.2% sales. 68 projects: 22% extensions, 45% platforms, 28% breakthroughs, 5% M&A.

AI with IBM Watson +40% formulation; Ginkgo FlexiCrunch chips 30% crunchier, 50% less fat, 8.7/10 sensory. Enzymatic PET recycling 90% by 2026.

Regional: NA 45% premium health PureFit $100M run-rate; EMEA 30% GreenWave pods €75M H1'25; APAC 20% ZestBurst India; LATAM 5% VitaFresh.

Pruned 150 SKUs, portfolio health 92%, 72% launches hit IRI targets. Expect 5-6 points 2025 growth, margins +200bps via ProcureAI -12% variances.

Now, market share trends reinforce this. Q3 +110 bps globally, 11th quarter, T12M 18.4% +80 bps YoY, IRI/Nielsen/e-comm.

Personal care +150 bps NA to 22.7%, FreshGuard whitening 31% vs. Colgate; natural rinses +5 points e-comm.

Home care +90 bps to 19.2%, TidePure 28% NA laundry +1.8 points eco-pods.

Beauty/grooming +120 bps to 15.8%, Pantene Renew 24% Europe hair.

Food/snacks +70 bps to 13.4%, NutriBar 11% healthy.

Health/wellness +200 bps to 16.1%, VitaBoost 19% gummies.

NA +140 bps to 24.6%, 92% club ACV. Europe +50 bps vs. discounters. APAC +220 bps China skincare. LATAM +90 bps.

Win with Precision: 15% trade to digital 2x ROI, Supply Chain 4.0 -35% OOS. 12 platforms 65% sustainable. FY +100-120 bps.

Our digital marketing drives engagement, strong from CrunchTime campaigns.

Following me, David will update on supply chain.

David Lopez:
Thank you, Lisa. We continue optimizing supply chain for efficiency and cost reduction. Implementing AI-driven demand sensing like Blue Yonder across 70% plants reduced inventory 12%, waste 8%. Factory utilization 88%, line speeds +15%. RSPO palm 95%, Vietnam expansions mitigate Red Sea. Global Supply Chain 2.0 with SAP/IoT cuts OOS to 2.5%. Project Horizon $450M savings, procurement with Cargill. Nearshoring LATAM $100M. Sustainability: 45% recycled content, PCR packaging, enzymatic recycling. Mitigating disruptions via multi-sourcing, $1.2B buffer.

Operator, we are now ready to open the call for questions.

Operator:
Thank you. Instructions: star one for questions. Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs.

John Smith:
Could you provide more insight into the geographic performance, particularly in emerging markets?

Mark Rivera:
Thanks, John. Emerging markets were a bright spot, contributing significantly to our 5.2% organic growth. Asia-Pacific accelerated to 5.6%, with China snacks up 12% volumes post-COVID, GlowEssence skincare to 18% share on Tmall. India oral care +180 bps rural via 1.2M village distribution, NutriBoost e-comm 35% penetration Shopee/Lazada 1.8 household points. LATAM +3.2% despite FX, Brazil snacks +2.5 points soccer promos, EcoShield 15% trial Mexico. Volume +4.2% emerging via micro-depots 45,000 outlets, pricing +3.7% compliance tech. Tailwinds from China reopening, $300M productivity offset inflation.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Davis with JPMorgan.

Emily Davis:
How are you managing inventory levels given the current economic uncertainty?

Sarah Thompson:
Good question, Emily. Inventory management is core to our resilience. AI demand sensing reduced levels 12% while cutting waste 8%, OOS to 2.5%. $1.2B buffer hedges geopolitics like Red Sea, Ukraine wheat. Right-sizing packs—20% more trial sizes—and e-comm 18% sales stabilize. Emerging micro-networks, NA hub-and-spoke consolidation. Utilization 88%, hedges 80% 2025 inputs. Balances volume +2.1% amid softness, supports Q4 4-6% organic.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mike Johnson with Morgan Stanley.

Mike Johnson:
Can you discuss the progress on your sustainability goals and any related cost implications?

David Lopez:
Absolutely, Mike. Sustainability drives share and margins. 45% recycled packaging on track for 50% 2025, boosting perception +12 points Kantar; 78% consumers prefer eco per Nielsen. RSPO palm 95% saves 2-3%, PCR 100% EcoShield/VitaGlow lifts repeats 22%. Enzymatic PET 90% circularity 2026 ahead Unilever. RSPO, ocean-bound plastics GreenWave comply EU Green Deal. Costs accretive: fermentation -18% ingredients, Project Horizon $450M includes joint R&D Cargill. Eco-refills +25% mix +50 bps premium.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Rachel Lee with Barclays.

Rachel Lee:
What are your expectations for pricing elasticity in the coming quarters?

Lisa Chen:
Thanks, Rachel. Pricing elasticity remains favorable. +2.5% Q3 with -0.3% volume drag vs. industry -1.2% Kantar, via Pricing Platform 50k scenarios. FY24 another 3-4%, NA +3.1% minimal pushback IRI penetration stable, EMEA 2-3% inflation. Mix-neutral protects premium. PCU >1.05x, cumulative +18% restores margins. Q4 +2-2.5%, elasticities modeled AI trade opti +12% ROI. Emerging +3.7% street-price tech 95% compliance. Holiday promos TPE 92%.

Operator:
There are no further questions at this time. I will now turn the call back to Mark Rivera for closing remarks.

Mark Rivera:
Thank you, Operator, and thank you all for your insightful questions. We remain committed to delivering strong results and creating value for our shareholders through innovation, disciplined execution, and share gains. Our launches, balanced growth levers, margin expansion, and efficient A&P position us to outperform in a challenging CPG landscape. We look forward to updating you on our progress next quarter.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes the Global Consumer Brands Inc. Q3 FY2024 Earnings Conference Call. You may now disconnect.
